```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
library(sciparseR)
```

An `sc_document` is a plain R list of data frames plus three metadata
lists. It is designed so that any element can be traced back to the
source file, and any later result can be traced back to an element.

```{r}
doc <- sc_parse(system.file("extdata", "single_column.pdf", package = "sciparseR"))
summary(doc)
```

## Entities

| Table | One row per | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `pages` | page | size, rotation, text layer, image-only flag, OCR status, columns |
| `spans` | word | coordinates, font, superscript flag, line and block, source, confidence |
| `lines` | text line segment | coordinates, font size, bold ratio |
| `blocks` | paragraph, heading, caption, table, figure, header, footer, ... | type, reading order, section, continuation |
| `sections` | heading | level, number, title, canonical label, parent |
| `tables`, `cells` | table, cell | spans, header flag, markers, missing tokens, continuation |
| `figures`, `captions` | figure, caption | region, label, target |
| `equations` | display equation | text, LaTeX and MathML when available, status |
| `footnotes` | footnote | scope (page or table), marker |
| `references`, `citations` | reference, citation | parsed fields, identifiers, link status |
| `supplementary` | supplementary file (JATS) | label, caption, link |
| `warnings` | parser warning | stage, code, page, element |

Every entity table has the same columns for every document, even when it
has no rows, so code written against one document works on all of them.

```{r}
names(doc$cells)
nrow(doc$cells)
```

## Identifiers

Identifiers are stable for a given file and configuration: parsing the
same file twice yields the same ids. They encode the page so that they
stay readable: `b-p002-0003` is the third block of page 2,
`t-p001-0001` the first table of page 1, `r-002` the second reference.
The document id is `doc-` followed by the first 16 hexadecimal digits of
the file's SHA-256.

```{r}
doc$doc_id
substr(doc$source$sha256, 1, 16)
identical(sc_parse(doc$source$path)$blocks$block_id, doc$blocks$block_id)
```

## Coordinates

Coordinates are PDF points (1/72 inch) with the origin at the top-left
corner of the page **as displayed**: `x0 < x1` from left to right and
`y0 < y1` from top to bottom. For pages with a `/Rotate` entry, the
coordinates refer to the upright page, which is what a reader sees and
what `sc_figure_crop()` and `sc_highlight()` render.

```{r}
sc_pages(doc)[, c("page", "width", "height", "rotation", "n_columns")]
sc_source(doc, "b-p001-0005")[, c("element_type", "page", "x0", "y0", "x1", "y1")]
```

JATS documents have no geometry. Their elements carry an XPath instead,
and all coordinate columns are `NA`. sciparseR never invents coordinates.

## Methods and statuses

Each block, table and figure records the method that produced it and a
status. The method says *how* it was found; the status says *how sure*
the parser is.

```{r}
unique(doc$blocks[, c("type", "method")])
```

Examples of statuses: a table continuation is `joined` only when the
caption says "continued" and the columns match, otherwise `possible`; an
equation without source markup has `latex_status = "not_reconstructed"`;
a page without a text layer has `ocr_status = "needed"`.

## Warnings

Problems are recorded instead of being hidden:

```{r}
scan <- sc_parse(system.file("extdata", "scanned.pdf", package = "sciparseR"))
scan$warnings
```

## Provenance of the run

```{r}
doc$source[c("file_name", "format", "size_bytes")]
doc$processing$config_hash
sc_config()
```

The configuration hash changes whenever any setting changes, which is how
the batch cache knows when a file has to be parsed again.
